inventory_duplicate_check.message: Review coverage and attach new evidence; no duplicate rule drafted.

rule_reviews.why_use: A web server process launching a command shell can indicate post-exploitation; deployments and maintenance can also cause this. Investigate parent lineage, account, command line, and change window.
rule_reviews.telemetry_needed: Sysmon Event ID 1 / DeviceProcessEvents / Splunk Sysmon process creation; Sigma/SPL Windows only

declared_telemetry_fit.sigma:
title: "Web Service Spawns a Shell"
id: 7443b43f-5c67-5545-85b2-381d9f4db20e
status: experimental
description: Behavior hypothesis; investigate correlated evidence before alerting.
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    "ParentImage|endswith": ["\\w3wp.exe", "\\httpd.exe", "\\nginx.exe"]
    "Image|endswith": ["\\cmd.exe", "\\powershell.exe"]
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Authorized administration or application maintenance
level: medium
declared_telemetry_fit.validation: Mapping declared only. A target-specific Sigma pipeline or manually reviewed query and native SIEM test are required; no local query is executed.
declared_telemetry_fit.next_step: Convert and test the Sigma rule with an appropriate backend, then import verified coverage.

source_evidence.claim: Synthetic lab analyst annotation: In this invented lab incident, w3wp.exe spawned cmd.exe after the attacker exploited CVE-2099-99999 on the exposed ExampleServer host. The process creation event preserved ParentImage, Image, CommandLine, timestamp, and account.

rule_reviews.further_attacker_adaptation_hypothesis: The attacker could start a different child such as rundll32.exe; separately assess web-worker lineage and DLL loads before widening the rule.
rule_reviews.adaptation_probability: not calibrated; investigate, do not present an invented number

rule_reviews.why_use: Encoded PowerShell commands can hide script content. Legitimate administration may also use encoding; review decoded content, signer, ancestry, and user context.
rule_reviews.telemetry_needed: Sysmon Event ID 1 / DeviceProcessEvents / Splunk Sysmon process creation with command line

declared_telemetry_fit.sigma:
title: "PowerShell Encoded Command Execution"
id: 9015d5b4-78bf-5644-be3e-b6fb74748ce1
status: experimental
description: Behavior hypothesis; investigate correlated evidence before alerting.
logsource:

  product: windows

  condition: selection
falsepositives:

level: medium

declared_telemetry_fit.next_step: Convert and test the Sigma rule with an appropriate backend, then import verified coverage.

source_evidence.claim: Synthetic lab analyst annotation: During the fictional intrusion, a signed powershell.exe process executed an -EncodedCommand payload after user sign-in. Process creation logging recorded the full command line, parent process, and user identity.

rule_reviews.further_attacker_adaptation_hypothesis: The attacker could change the argument syntax or use another script host; validate observed command-line variants and decoded content before expanding detection.
rule_reviews.adaptation_probability: not calibrated; investigate, do not present an invented number

rule_reviews.why_use: A tool marked executed despite a non-allow authorization decision is a policy-state mismatch. Investigate request binding, delayed decisions, log completeness, and idempotent retries; this alert alone does not prove compromise.
rule_reviews.telemetry_needed: Custom MCP audit contract: event_type, execution_status, authorization_decision, principal_id, request_id, tool_name, resource_scope, timestamp

declared_telemetry_fit.sigma:
title: "MCP Tool Executed Without Allow Decision"
id: 9cc82294-52e5-5d53-9ad9-4b18800bca09
status: experimental
description: Behavior hypothesis; investigate correlated evidence before alerting.
logsource:
  category: application
  product: mcp_audit
detection:
  selection:
    "event_type": "tool_invocation"
    "execution_status": "executed"
    "authorization_decision": ["deny", "missing", "expired"]
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Authorized administration or application maintenance
level: medium
declared_telemetry_fit.validation: Mapping declared only. A target-specific Sigma pipeline or manually reviewed query and native SIEM test are required; no local query is executed.
declared_telemetry_fit.next_step: Convert and test the Sigma rule with an appropriate backend, then import verified coverage.

source_evidence.claim: Synthetic lab analyst annotation: The MCP tool invocation executed even though its authorization decision was deny for the same request ID. Audit events included execution status, principal ID, tool name, resource scope, and timestamp.

rule_reviews.further_attacker_adaptation_hypothesis: An attacker could evade a single audit source or race authorization state; correlate the enforcement decision and execution receipt using the same request ID.

tuning_notes: E02 and E04 need change-window, signer, ancestry, and decoded-command review; suppressing all such traffic could conceal malicious use.
E08 and E09 are deliberate misses. Investigate these telemetry variants as separately evidenced hypotheses; do not infer coverage from a title or one lab sample.
MCP E05 is a policy mismatch; verify request binding and independent enforcement records before calling it an intrusion.
